text:
Anya M: Ran A100 vs H100 iso sweep for LLM-7B (prefill+decode) across us-west-2 / eu-west-1 / us-east-1. Putting raw highlights here so infra/product can react.

Samir: Nice — what hardware SKUs and quant configs?

Anya M: H100s (H100-PCIe 80GB) vs A100 40GB. Tests: fp16 baseline, q4_0 & q8_0 variants. Sequence lengths 512/1024/2048 to cover chat and long-context. Batches tuned for 99ms p99 latency target.

perf-bot: upload complete: s3://redwood-bench/bench-1848765432 (run id: run-1848765432-a)

Samir: Paste of the summarized table (tokens/sec = decode-only at steady-state, prefill = prefill-only throughput):

A100 (40GB) | H100 (80GB) | notes
-------------------------------------------
prefill tok/s (seq1024) | 3200 tok/s | 5200 tok/s | H100 + better prefill kernel + improved GEMM paths
decode tok/s (seq1024)  | 2100 tok/s | 3300 tok/s | H100 speedup ~1.55x
$/1M tokens (fp16)      | $7.8       | $5.2       | region pricing + effective tokens/sec
$/1M tokens (q4_0)      | $4.6       | $3.0       | quant gains, model accuracy checked on eval set

Marta: Where did you get $/1M? Cloud list price + pool utilization assumptions?

Anya M: Yes — per-GPU hourly cost (on-demand) + tokens/sec measured at steady-state with batching. Assumptions in s3 run meta: 85% effective utilization, 10% overhead for routing. Link in perf-bot artifact.

Kevin: Observed one weird thing in eu-west: H100 decode p99 tail (~99th pct) jumps to ~310ms for seq2048 in 2/20 runs. A100 stayed around 410ms median but lower tail variance. Logs attached in s3. Could be network hiccup or NUMA config.

Samir: Can you paste the p50/p95/p99 breakdown for decode seq2048?

Anya M: Sure:

H100 seq2048 decode: p50=70ms, p95=160ms, p99=320ms
A100 seq2048 decode: p50=95ms, p95=175ms, p99=420ms

Anya M: So H100 wins on median and p95, but has sporadic p99 spikes. Need to triage whether those are kernel-level or infra.

Marta: Did you run with kernel selection set to "auto"? Which kernels were chosen?

Anya M: Auto. Observed kernel map: prefill on H100 -> cuBLAS/FlashAttention-optimized GEMM (new kernel family), decode -> tensorkernel fused op for attention + KVcache. A100 mostly used cutlass-based kernels and older attention path.

Samir: Did you try forcing the "legacy" kernels on H100 to compare stability?

Anya M: Yes, forced legacy paths on H100 and spikes disappeared but median dropped ~12%. So tradeoff: new kernels faster but have rare outliers.

Kevin: Could be driver/GPU power management interplay. Any GPU-side logs (nv-hostengine, nsys)?

Anya M: Collected nsys traces for a couple of the spike runs and uploaded to s3. Early look suggests a long memcpy stall during a particular iteration in the sequence where KV size crosses a threshold (~1.9M entries).

perf-bot: artifact: s3://redwood-bench/bench-1848765432/traces/ (nsys + perf counters)

Marta: On quantization: q4_0 quality drop on our eval set was <0.8% exact-match for standard QA prompts, q8_0 ~0.2%. q4 gave ~40% lower $/1M tokens compared to fp16 on A100.

Samir: Nice. For product-facing pricing we should use the H100 q4_0 numbers if we can mitigate p99 spikes. Can you run a canary with kernel pinning but with our prefetch tweaks?

Anya M: Plan: run a 48-hour regional canary in us-west with H100, kernel auto but enable prefetch KV and enable pinned-mem allocator. Command I used for single-run repro:

```
./run_bench --model llama-7b --seq 2048 --gpu h100 --quant q4_0 --batch 8 --kernel auto --prefetch-kv --pinned-mem
```

Samir: Add `--trace-interval 500` to collect more frequent micro-traces for the tail events.

Anya M: Will do. Spawning 48h canary now. run id: run-1848765432-b (linked in perf-bot)

deploy-bot: Canary started: run-1848765432-b on pool-h100-us-west-2 (48h) :rocket:

Kevin: Also, for capacity planning: with conservative stable numbers (use H100 median tokens/sec), we'd size N GPUs for XQPS. I'll post a calced sheet after canary.

Marta: For the public docs we should note: typical H100 improvements 1.4-1.7x vs A100 for 7B prefill+decode, but call out tail outliers and kernel tradeoffs. Keep language conservative.

Anya M: Agreed. I'll add a short PR to the benchmarks repo with updated numbers + a short note about p99 behaviors and mitigation steps. :memo: 

Samir: Thanks — this is very helpful. @perf-bot please set an alert if p99 > 300ms for more than 5% of requests on the canary.

perf-bot: alert rule created: canary/run-1848765432-b p99>300ms for 5% windows.

Anya M: Leaving logs and quick repro in s3. Will update after 12h mark. :eyes:
